entry.title: bitcoindev@googlegroups.com
entry.summary:
The recent discussions on the implementation of an unspendable NUMS key specifically for script path only taproot policy have led to a set of guidelines and technical specifics aimed at standardizing this approach. The primary source for these details includes discussions on forums such as [Delving Bitcoin](https://delvingbitcoin.org/t/unspendable-keys-in-descriptors/304) and a pull request on [GitHub](https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/pull/1746). These platforms have outlined the methodology and rationale behind the proposed changes.
The approach adopted does not enforce strict adherence to other Bitcoin Improvement Proposals (BIPs) unless they are directly relevant to the current issue. Instead, it leverages existing mechanisms from other BIPs, avoiding the semantic canonicalization of the script while still normalizing the policy to a certain degree. A new placeholder, denoted as "_", is introduced in the descriptor to represent the unspendable NUMS key. This facilitates the organization and sorting of keys within musig() and sortedmulti_a structures, as well as the sibling pairs of the tree. In cases where a multipath extension is present, a tuple of the same length is added to the placeholder to prevent key reuse.
Furthermore, the extraction and utilization of keys involve using "@i" placeholders followed by hashing the entire arrangement, which includes both the normalized descriptor and the keys. This process generates the chain code as per the specifications in BIP 341. More comprehensive details and technical documentation can be found in the proposal hosted on GitHub under the file [bip-xxxx-unspendable-internal-keys.mediawiki](https://github.com/bitryonix/bips/blob/bip-xxxx-unspendable-internal-keys/bip-xxxx-unspendable-internal-keys.mediawiki). This proposal aims to enhance the security and efficiency of taproot transactions by preventing the misuse of internal keys while maintaining a structured and systematic framework for their implementation.
